title: The Anatomy of a Thriving Innovation Ecosystem

We are here to tackle the anatomy of a thriving innovation system, the ecosystem. And we have the absolute best in the business to talk about it. So, let's
welcome Helmut Schönenberger, the co-founder and CEO of UnternehmerTUM, Jüri Ratas, co-founder and executive chairman at the Delta, Mats Kuuskemaa, country director, Government of Estonia,
Fanny Jiménez, VP Performance and Collaboration at Premium Group A. So, let's welcome on the stage >> [laughter] >> Good morning, everyone. Welcome to this exciting panel.
>> [sighs] >> It's going to be fun. And if you have questions, think about them already. We reserved 5 minutes at the end for your questions, and it's a very
unique opportunity because we have as you just heard, some very special people here. We will talk about innovation systems, thriving innovation systems. And each of

how innovation becomes repeatable. Uh Jüri Ratas, you're in my opinion the founder and company builder. I'm hoping to see from you uh the the

um what does UnternehmerTUM actually build? How do you do it? >> Cool. Funny. Great to be here. So, what's what's such an ecosystem? And

>> It's people, guys like you, Julian. So, it's all about people, all about talent and so as an UnternehmerTUM is an entrepreneurship center startup factory and so our
our special skill is not to see Julian that he's now a great entrepreneur, but Julian 10 or 15 years ago, okay? When he was more like a kid

With and with our university, so we um we are backed by TUM, which is a leading university with 50,000 students, 10,000 researchers, and I my team is about 500

it's extremely easy to set up a company, it costs almost nothing. People can have three companies if they want to, even a freelancers. They they don't think twice

to to be an entrepreneur because then you will get more more startups, more unicorns. And we have the highest per capita than Europe about.
>> Mhm. Wow. And your new record, tell us about the new record and why it's important. >> That's right. So we have around more
than 40,000 companies that are established by e-residents and it's around 3,150 by Germans. So it's it's quite a bit for Estonia. So So many Germans also found
Estonia as an extra tool to kind of have the easy way to to start their business. >> Mhm. >> May I ask questions about my tax and how
does it work? So if I'm now here a developer in Berlin and I I want to found a company, so how does it work practically and also
with relating to tax? So how is the tax relationship in Estonia and how is my local tax relationship? >> So Estonia would do like a quick
background check on you, check if you have any criminal records and things like this. But so that everyone's in a good club and then we have a marketplace

a plan if you found a company abroad, right? Either if you you're planning to move out of Germany or live in Estonia, that's very easy case. But if you live
in Germany, you should build some substance for a company in Estonia as well. So you can justify that it would be taxed in in Estonian system.
>> Mhm. Mhm. And one backup question, why is Estonia doing this? What does the country gain from it? >> That's actually we often get this
question, but I think the main thing is actually the diversity because we joke that we have really worse winters than Berlin does. So so people can be part of
our ecosystem but not necessarily live there. So around 40% of our startups have e-resident founders. So all these diversities like bringing us a lot of
value and and also in the end some of these companies hire people locally and that's how Estonia benefits. >> Yeah. Thank you. You said just now that the
tax system is one of the reasons why people don't found here for example and also the financial risks. And what I want to ask you
money is important, of course, but in your experience what matters more than money? >> So what matters more is money is definitely important okay?
Especially if you build large companies, you need money, okay? And you need great people. You know, and you said you had to meet people,
employees, co-founders. So you need to be in the such an ecosystem as Delta where you meet people, okay? And have great co-founders. It's like marrying a
person okay? >> [laughter] >> And then you need customers basically who pay you. And last but not least, you also have the infrastructure and that the talent

know the routines. You You have all the service providers who do it. You have a pool of talented people who are in finance and HR and so

because Mats, we also in the prep talk, we talked about agents. And maybe Julian, you can also think about how it matters for your experiences.
>> Yeah, I just quickly wanted to jump in that the hunger part is also really important because you know, often founders, they they can get really good

to have our first unicorn Skype in 2005. And it was one of the first in Europe actually. And we had like this employee stock option system that has been really
